admitted.name: no_numbers_in_person_field
admitted.rationale: The 'person' field should not contain entities with numeric characters, as names typically do not include numbers.

admitted.name: locations_are_geographical_entities
admitted.rationale: Entities in the 'location' field should represent geographical locations. Non-geographical entities like people's names or organizations are incorrect in this field.

admitted.name: no_empty_strings_in_fields
admitted.rationale: Fields should not contain empty strings as entities. Empty strings indicate a parsing error.

admitted.name: numeric_entities_in_else_only
admitted.rationale: Entities containing numeric values should only appear in the 'else' field, as such entities are unlikely to represent people, locations, or organizations.

admitted.name: person_field_contains_human_names
admitted.rationale: The 'person' field should contain entities that could plausibly be human names. Entities like 'Cup' or 'Ministry' do not belong here.

admitted.name: organization_field_contains_institutions
admitted.rationale: The 'organization' field should only contain entities that represent institutions or groups. Non-institutional entities, like 'Hungary' or 'Shehu', are incorrect here.

admitted.name: else_not_overlap_with_other_fields
admitted.rationale: Entities in the 'else' field should not appear in any other field, as they are meant to capture distinct types of entities.

admitted.name: substring_case_insensitive
admitted.rationale: Every gold entity is an exact substring of the text, and the label compares lower-cased values. So every correct entity is a case-insensitive substring of the text. This catches invented or paraphrased entities.

admitted.name: token_aligned
admitted.rationale: CoNLL entities are spans of whole tokens, so a correct entity must match a contiguous token sequence of the text (case-insensitive). This catches partial-token extractions.

admitted.name: entity_has_letter
admitted.rationale: Named entities contain letters. This catches numbers, scores and dates extracted as entities, such as "1", "0-0" and "1996-08-26".

admitted.name: count_le_occurrences
admitted.rationale: Each gold entity is a distinct span of the text. So an entity string cannot appear across all fields more times than it occurs in the text. This catches the same span being duplicated or assigned to several types.

admitted.name: no_leading_lowercase_article
admitted.rationale: CoNLL spans exclude a lowercase leading "the", "a" or "an" (for example "the Dodgers" is gold "Dodgers"). The check only rejects when every text occurrence starts with the lowercase article.

admitted.name: max_entity_length
admitted.rationale: CoNLL entities are short, essentially always 12 tokens or fewer. This catches whole clauses extracted as a single entity.

admitted.name: total_le_capitalized_tokens
admitted.rationale: Each gold entity is a non-overlapping span containing at least one token with an uppercase letter. So the total entity count cannot exceed the number of such tokens. This catches over-generation.

admitted.name: no_weekday_entity
admitted.rationale: CoNLL does not tag days of the week. This catches "Monday" or "Saturday" extracted as an entity.

admitted.name: no_pronoun_title_entity
admitted.rationale: Pronouns and bare titles are never CoNLL entities on their own. This catches entries like "He", "President" or "Minister".

admitted.name: no_date_pattern
admitted.rationale: CoNLL does not tag dates. This catches strings like "1996-08-26" or "08/26/96".

admitted.name: lowercase_text_empty
admitted.rationale: If the text has no uppercase letter at all, it contains no capitalized named entity. So every field must be empty, and any extraction is rejected.

admitted.name: no_time_token
admitted.rationale: Clock times are not named entities. This catches tokens like "10:30", "GMT 1430" style pieces, or "a.m." / "p.m." inside an entity.

admitted.name: no_all_lowercase_multiword_else
admitted.rationale: A multi-word "else" entry where every text occurrence is fully lowercase cannot be a named entity. This specifically catches phrases like "alien-led profit boost".

admitted.name: no_number_only_token_edges
admitted.rationale: Entity spans essentially never end with a pure-number token, so a trailing number signals an over-extended span (for example "Hungary 1"). Leading numbers are allowed because names like "1860 Munich" exist.
